intro_text: I've been on every side of this fence; from a business perspective. Content Production, Retail Distribution, Technology Provider, Brands, Professional and Consumer. Threading the needle is not trivial.

squares.text:
The Consumer Audio market is one of the oldest consumer tech markets.

Every existing Technology and Product Segment is a quagmire; veterans have 'seen it all'. 

Our products have to be compelling alternatives to what's available. 

But different enough to stand out. 

But not so different that partners and customers can't easily spot the value proposition.

Google/Meta/Amazon ad-spend can be a crippling obligation for a start up brand. 

AGF and it's products need to be exciting enough to generate buzz:

Channels: An exciting brand story and profitable to sell. 

Media: Newsworthy so reviewers are eager to cover them. 

 Customers: Are drawn in by the promise of a new brand truly doing new things - that they can't get anywhere else.

AGF needs every element of it's strategy to be sticky, and defensible.  

A savage and relentless campaign on every obvious place the industry is asleep at the wheel. 

A seductive and confident beacon of hope to taste makers in adjacent industries.

A welcoming new community focal point for music loving technology enthusiasts, globally.

summary: As scary as that list looks in aggregate, I assure you, this is not a 'boil the ocean' plan. The dots connected when trying to figure out how to contextualize B&O's old distribution model, how to provision physical space for operations, and R&D relationships for our primary technology differentiators. The costs will be lower than a traditional route, we just need to have the courage to lead; let's connect the dots.
